Simplify the following powers of \(i\).

  • \(i^{18}=\)
  • \(i^{20}=\)
  • \(i^{47}=\)
  • \(i^{60}=\)
  • \(i^{85}=\)

For any positive integer \(n\), we can evaluate \(i^n\) by determining the remainder when \(n\) is divided by 4.

Remainder of \(n/4\) \(i^n\)
0 \(1\)
1 \(i\)
2 \(-1\)
3 \(-i\)

In computer programming, the modulo operator returns the remainder. This operation is used so frequently, that it is often abbreviated to a single symbol (for example, in Python, 5%2 represents the remainder when 5 is divided by 2.)

I will represent the remainders using the Desmos notation.

  • \(\mathrm{mod}(18,4)=2\) so \(i^{18}=-1\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(20,4)=0\) so \(i^{20}=1\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(47,4)=3\) so \(i^{47}=-i\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(60,4)=0\) so \(i^{60}=1\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(85,4)=1\) so \(i^{85}=i\)

To find the remainder using a scientific calculator, I would divide by 4, floor the result, multiply by 4, and subtract that amount from the original.

\[\mathrm{mod}(x,4)~=~x-4\cdot \left\lfloor\frac{x}{4}\right\rfloor\]

Simplify the following radical expression.

\[\sqrt{-80}\]

\[\sqrt{-80}\]

Use prime factorization.

\[\sqrt{(-1)\cdot 2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot5}\]

Isolate twins.

\[\sqrt{2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot (-1)\cdot 5}\]

\[\sqrt{16}\cdot \sqrt{-1}\cdot \sqrt{5}\]

\[4i \sqrt{5}\]
